messages.subject: group by detector covariates
messages.body_plain:
Hi All -

I have small mammal mark-recapture data and I'm trying to set-up/run a model that varies grouped by covariates on the detectors/traps. I have the 2.9.2 update secr pkg.

The script I'm running is:
>Capt.Object<- read.table("Captures.txt",header = TRUE)
>Trap.Object<-read.traps("Detectors.txt", detector="multi", covnames =c("Gd", "ShbCnt", "ShbRich", "CpyAr"))
>pkmTest4<-make.capthist(Capt.Object, Trap.Object,fmt = "trapID", noccasions=3)
>secr.modelgrid <- secr.fit (pkmTest4, model = list(D~g, g0~g), groups = "Gd")

The error message I get when I run the secr.fit line is:
> Error in `[.data.frame`(covariates(capthist), , groups) :
  undefined columns selected

I don't think I'm setting up or calling the covariates correctly, but I'm not sure what else to try. I've also attached the two data files, if that is helpful.

Any suggestions or advice would be greatly appreciated!

Best,

Sarah

messages.subject: RE: group by detector covariates
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sarah,

Here is an attempt to getting you going.

First, I think you are looking to model detection using trap level covariates (Gd), or at least, that how I interpreted it. Specifying ‘~g’ in the model is reserved for covariates that group individuals (i.e. it is basically an individual covariate). So, instead what you can do is model detection directly as a function of trap covariates – in your case g0~Gd.

The files you sent had some text at the bottom that gave me some problems until I realized what was going on.

Here is what I did:

# make the capthist object in one step directly rather than a few:

Capt.Object<- read.capthist("Captures.txt","Detectors.txt",trapcovnames=c("Gd", "ShbCnt", "ShbRich", "CpyAr"))

summary(Capt.Object)

# fit a model allowing detection to vary with ‘Gd’

secr.modelgrid <- secr.fit (Capt.Object,g0~Gd)

#I wasn’t sure what you were going for by modelling density by group as you didn’t

#have an individual covariate in there but you could have session specific density:

secr.modelgrid <- secr.fit (Capt.Object, list(D~session, g0~Gd))

Hope that helps a little?

Chris

messages.subject: Re: group by detector covariates
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sarah

Groups are defined on individual covariates: secr.fit looks for an individual covariate called 'Gd' and doesn't find one.

I see you want to model grid-level differences in both density and detection parameters. Groups are not suitable for grid-level (spatial) comparisons of density - they refer to co-occurring subpopulations. I suggest you define new 'sessions' as a combination of the current session and Gd. Then you will have complete flexibility to model 'session' level differences in density and detection parameters.

Here is some fairly obscure code that does that. It's not the end of your problems, because there are two grid x sess combinations with no detections. I thought that secr.fit could handle that, but it doesn't, so I'll have to investigate more. Otherwise, it looks like a nice dataset.

## split capthist by grid as well as sess
tmp <- list()
for (i in 1:6)
  tmp <- c(tmp, split(pkmTest4[[i]], f = covariates(traps(pkmTest4))[[i]]$Gd,
                                   bytrap = T))
CH <- MS.capthist(tmp)
sessiondata <- expand.grid( grid = c('A','B','C'), sess = 1:6)
head(sessiondata)

session(CH) <-  apply(sessiondata, 1, paste, collapse='')
summary(CH, terse = T)
#            A1 B1 C1 A2 B2 C2 A3 B3 C3 A4 B4 C4 A5 B5 C5 A6 B6 C6
# Occasions   3  3  3  3  3  3  3  3  3  3  3  3  3  3  3  3  3  3
# Detections 14  9 15 18  0  0  7 11  1 17 21  5 25 15  4 30 17 35
# Animals     7  6  8 16  0  0  6 11  1 11 12  5 13  8  3 18  7 19
# Detectors  64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64 64

## secr.fit seems to choke on the sessions (grids) with no captures,
## even if verify = FALSE, so drop these for now...
CH2 <- subset(CH, sessions=c(1:4,7:18), dropnullocc = FALSE)
sessiondata2 <- sessiondata[-(5:6),]

## starting values can be a problem with multiple sessions, so we specify them
## this model assumes density and detection constant over time (sess = 1:6),
## and sigma constant over both time and grids
secr.modelgrid <- secr.fit (CH2, model = list(D~grid, g0~grid), sessioncov = sessiondata2,
  start = c(D=log(20), 0, 0, g0=logit(.05), 0, 0, sigma=log(10)), buffer = 50)

predict(secr.modelgrid)
# $`session = A1, grid = A`
# link   estimate SE.estimate         lcl        ucl
# D       log 11.0460912  1.61645293  8.30434722 14.6930431
# g0    logit  0.1292909  0.02275492  0.09084064  0.1807799
# sigma   log 11.9754701  0.77005562 10.55879667 13.5822186
#
# $`session = B1, grid = B`
# link   estimate SE.estimate        lcl        ucl
# D       log  7.8411870  1.37768737  5.5713698 11.0357445
# g0    logit  0.1692654  0.03853805  0.1064044  0.2585195
# sigma   log 11.9754701  0.77005562 10.5587967 13.5822186
#
# $`session = C1, grid = C`
# link   estimate SE.estimate        lcl        ucl
# D       log  5.9261173  1.12199417  4.1023126  8.5607485
# g0    logit  0.1973613  0.04601297  0.1221555  0.3028925
# sigma   log 11.9754701  0.77005562 10.5587967 13.5822186
## etc.

Murray

P.S. If you comment out the header line in your captures file you can do all the input with one statement:

pkmTest4 <- read.capthist('Captures.txt', 'Detectors.txt',
      trapcovnames = c("Gd", "ShbCnt", "ShbRich", "CpyAr"),
      fmt = "trapID", noccasions = 3)

Updating my earlier reply -
I have tweaked the secr code to better handle sessions with no detections. The Windows binary and source code for this 'under development' version secr 2.9.3 are downloadable from http://www.otago.ac.nz/density/SECRinR.html. In Windows, use 'Packages | Install package(s) from local zip file(s)'.

Now I get...
secr.modelgrid0 <- secr.fit (CH, model = list(D~grid, g0~grid), sessioncov = sessiondata,
            start = list(D=20, g0=0.05, sigma=10), buffer = 50, verify = FALSE)

predict(secr.modelgrid0)

# $`session = A1, grid = A`
# link   estimate SE.estimate         lcl       ucl

#

# D       log  4.9187496   0.9322275  3.403703  7.1081695

# sigma   log 12.0382970   0.7782722 10.606999 13.6627335
# etc.
Note we still have to override the pesky verify error. I hope it's all smooth sailing from here!
Murray

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am running some multi-session models with detection(g0) varying among some sessions. For Session 1 there was a treatment and I am trying to use 2 groups for detection, before and after the treatment. Here is my input:

secr_Dnull <- secr.fit(SAVRcap, model = list(D~1, g0~ab, sigma~1), trace=FALSE, verify=TRUE, mask=maskSAV, timecov = data.frame(ab = c('a','a','a','a','a','a','a','b','b','b','b','b','b','b','b','b','b','b','b','b','b','b','b','b', 'c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c', 'c','c','c', 'c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c', 'c','c','c', 'c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c', 'c','c','c', 'c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c','c', 'c','c','c')), ncores=4)

There are 24 occasions for each of the 5 sessions, hence the long list (maybe there is an easier way to code this?).

secr.fit runs (output below), but I'm not sure if the output is correct (which is why I'm not sure if I'm coding the covariate correctly). g0 is the same for all sessions and it should be different for session 1 vs. 2-5. The output shows ab=a for all the sessions, so it looks like it ran as g0~1.

Also, the output gives 1 estimate of g0 for each session. If g0 is different for different occasions within a session, is there a way to view the 2 different estimates of g0 within 1 session?

Have a great day and thanks for any help anyone can provide!

-Wes

messages.subject: Re: secr.test and overdispersion
messages.body_plain:
To be clear, and to encourage others to reply: secr.test is just a way to simulate data under the model, re-fit the model, and collect some statistic(s) (default deviance/df). You could use the ratio of observed to simulated deviance/df to estimate a c-hat-like variance inflation factor, but that will combine  all sorts of model mis-specification and overdispersion, not just grouping of individuals. It's not guaranteed to be a good estimate. To my knowledge no-one has yet addressed overdispersion in SECR models - do you have (a lot of) time on your hands? :-)
Murray

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Thanks for responding, Murray.  I might be able to devote some time to this problem.  In camera-trapping surveys of primates, multiple individuals are frequently detected in a single photo or video.   I'm also aware that lack of model structure can contribute to overdispersion and that it could be difficult to separate sources of overdispersion in real data. We could probably simulate data where overdispersion results only from grouping of individuals, and otherwise the data conform to the specified model(?).
Eric

messages.subject: Re: secr.test and overdispersion
messages.body_plain:
Good that you may be able to look at overdispersion - certainly crops up with social species (wolves etc.). Your particular problem (group photos) sounds to me like one that could be tackled directly rather than via this indirect route. Note the clone() function in 'secr'. This generates overdispersion with constant, Poisson or binomial number per cluster; there is a default method and one for 'popn' objects (I was interested in multiple sounds from a point), but not currently one to replicate rows of capthist objects. I'll fix that when I get a chance.
Murray
